newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Tight supplies boost sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Tight supplies boost sentiment.

text.p: Tighter summer supplies from the Middle East supported sentiment in the Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market on Tuesday and traders expected the uptrend momentum to continue amid fresh buying support.
The 180-cst grade was offered/bid at $103.50 per tonne for different delivery dates, traders said.
A Singapore trader has bought three cargoes since last week, with the last one bought at $103.50 per tonne on Monday.
"It looks like he is still pretty interested in buying," said one trader.
The purchase emerged at a time when supplies from the Middle East started to decrease due to the summer demand there.
"There is no additional supplies from the Middle East, so prices should remain firm," said one trader.
However, traders agreed that the 180-cst grade would not exceed $105.00 per tonne, seen as a barrier for the cargo market's recent gains.
In the swaps market, June swaps were last quoted at $101.75/$102.50 per tonne, up from Monday's $101/$102, also amid fresh buying support.
Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) has issued a tender to sell a third 30,000-tonne cargo of 3.0-percent sulphur fuel oil for June lifting.
The tender to sell the 180-cst cargo for June 9-18 lifting will close on May 26 and will be valid for two days.
CPC will close its outstanding import tender for one or two cargoes of 0.5-percent fuel oil for July delivery on May 21. The tender is valid for two days.
Demand for the LSWR still did not pick up, but expectations for Japan's summer demand to pick up soon supported prices at above $15.00 per tonne, traders said.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
